comment.body: Thanks for identifying that Microsoft.CommandPalette.Extensions 0.12.260812002 introduces a .NET 10 requirement for an older-targeted extension project. To determine whether this is a package payload or project configuration problem, please share a minimal project file, its target framework, package reference and NuGet sources, plus the complete restore or build error. Please also retest with the current SDK/release and say whether the failure happens during restore, compilation, or runtime. If possible, include the package nuspec and the toolkit DLL/deps metadata from the installed package.

actions.note: Draft only; no upstream comment is posted without explicit approval.

judgment.rationale: The issue has no reproducible consumer project, complete error, package contents, or attachment. The source tree at the issue date exposes a plausible net10 build versus net8 package-metadata mismatch, but it cannot prove that the published 0.12.260812002 payload or the reporter's failure follows that path.
evidence: The report identifies SDK version 0.12.260812002 and says it forces .NET 10 on projects using older .NET versions.
The issue has no expected or actual behavior, numbered reproduction, project file, restore/build output, reporter follow-up, or attachment.
No assignee, linked pull request, project item, duplicate, or existing fork implementation covers the report.

At the issue date, src/Common.Dotnet.props set CoreTargetFramework to net10.0; src/Common.Dotnet.CsWinRT.props imported it; and the toolkit project imported the CsWinRT props without a TargetFramework override.

At the issue date, Microsoft.CommandPalette.Extensions.SDK.nuspec still declared net8.0-windows10.0.19041.0 and placed the toolkit DLL and deps file in that lib folder, while BuildSDKHelper.ps1 packed the files without target-framework validation.
judgment.recommended_action: Request the minimal failing project, complete restore/build output, retest result, and package metadata before designing or implementing a fix.

fix_assessment.rationale: No concrete PowerToys code change is responsibly selectable yet: an implementation would have to choose between restoring net8 compatibility, correcting package metadata, or fixing a separate restore/configuration fault without evidence identifying which is present.

issue_context.summary: The reporter says a Command Palette Extension SDK package associated with PowerToys 0.101 forces .NET 10 on an older-targeted extension project, but provides no consumer project, error output, or package artifact.
known_information: The reported package version is Microsoft.CommandPalette.Extensions 0.12.260812002.
The issue is about SDK package consumption, not a PowerToys runtime failure.
The upstream issue is open with Issue-Bug, Needs-Triage, and Product-Command Palette labels; it has no assignee or linked pull request.
The only discussion is an automated request for concrete reproduction details and a retest on the latest stable release.
The source at the issue date built the toolkit through shared net10 properties while the SDK nuspec advertised net8 asset paths.
inferences: The package may contain a net10-built managed toolkit or deps payload under net8 metadata.
The observed source mismatch is not sufficient to exclude a NuGet restore, SDK installation, package-reference, or consumer-project cause.
issue_context.analysis: The build import chain and nuspec make target-framework drift a credible hypothesis, but the published package and failure surface were not available to inspect. A detailed framework-retargeting design would select behavior before proving the failing artifact or compatibility contract.
initial_investigation: Read the complete live issue body, its only comment, labels, assignees, timeline, attachments, linked pull requests, project items, duplicate candidates, and related Command Palette SDK work.
Checked MuyuanMS/PowerToys for existing Issue 50235 traces; fork issue 584 is the sole mirror and has no implementation pull request.
Inspected the issue-date source import chain, toolkit project, SDK nuspec, SDK packaging script, pipeline template, and .NET 10 migration history.
Attempted to retrieve the exact public package for direct inspection, but the package host TLS handshake failed in this environment.

information_gaps.information: A minimal failing extension project with target framework, package reference, NuGet sources, and complete restore/build output
information_gaps.why_needed: It identifies whether .NET 10 is introduced during restore, compilation, or runtime and rules out consumer configuration causes.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Create a minimal project that reproduces the problem, include its project file, then paste the complete restore or build command output.

information_gaps.how_to_collect: Download or inspect the installed package and provide the nuspec, lib-folder listing, Microsoft.CommandPalette.Extensions.Toolkit.deps.json runtime target, and assembly target-framework metadata.

information_gaps.why_needed: It establishes whether the package problem remains active and which supported compatibility contract a fix must preserve.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Update the SDK/release, repeat the minimal reproduction, and report the SDK version plus whether restore, compilation, or runtime fails.

design.root_cause: Not established. The package target-framework mismatch is a qualified hypothesis only.

evidence.detail: The issue-date build import chain sets the toolkit target through shared net10 properties, while the nuspec advertises net8 assets.
The issue does not provide the failing project, full error, or published package contents.
A net10 toolkit payload under net8 metadata could cause the reported compatibility failure, but this has not been verified against package version 0.12.260812002.

affected_files.purpose: Defines the shared CoreTargetFramework consumed by the SDK toolkit import chain.
Imports the shared framework properties for CsWinRT consumers.
Consumes the shared build properties and produces the managed toolkit payload.
Declares the package dependency group and lib asset folder.
Builds the toolkit and packs it without inspecting emitted framework metadata.

verify: Inspect the reported package's nuspec, lib asset folder, toolkit assembly TargetFrameworkAttribute, and toolkit deps runtime target.
Restore and build the reporter's minimal older-framework extension project with its recorded package source and version.
Compare the observed failure with a package built from the issue-date source before choosing a source or packaging change.
risks: Retargeting the toolkit to net8 without confirming the supported SDK contract could introduce compilation or runtime incompatibilities.
Changing only NuGet metadata could make package compatibility declarations accurate while preserving the reported break for older consumers.
A framework change affects CsWinRT-generated and native runtime asset packaging, so validation must include the actual package.
alternatives: Do not implement an explicit net8 retarget until package contents and the failing consumer prove that net8 compatibility is intended and broken.
Do not retarget package metadata to net10 as a workaround until maintainers confirm that dropping older consumers is an intentional support decision.

adversary.verdict: Blocking objection: no independent package payload or failing consumer evidence establishes the proposed root cause.
